raunch someone out†.monolingual: Sl. to disgust someone. _These dirty socks absolutely raunch me out! _ Sam and Beavis enjoy raunching out everyone in the room.
examples: Sam and Beavis enjoy raunching out everyone in the room.

rave about someone or something.monolingual: 1. to rage in anger about someone or something. _ Gale was raving about Sarah and what she did. _ Sarah raved and raved about Gale’s insufferable rudeness.
examples: Gale was raving about Sarah and what she did.

rave over someone or something.monolingual: to recite praises for someone or something. _The students were just raving over the new professor. _ Donald raved over the cake I baked. But he’ll eat anything.
examples: The students were just raving over the new professor.

ravished with delight.monolingual: Fig. happy or delighted; overcome with happiness or delight. _ Mary was ravished with delight by the dozen roses. _My parents were ravished with delight when I graduated from college.
examples: Mary was ravished with delight by the dozen roses.

*a raw deal.monolingual: an instance of unfair or bad treatment. (*Typically: get ~; have ~; give someone ~.) _ Mary got a raw deal on her traffic ticket. She was innocent, but she had to pay a big fine. _I bought a used TV that worked for two days and then quit. I sure got
examples: Mary got a raw deal on her traffic ticket.

raw recruit.monolingual: a new, inexperienced, or fresh recruit, such as someone just entering the army, navy, police, etc. _These boys are nothing but raw recruits. They’ve never seen a gun up close!
examples: These boys are nothing but raw recruits.

raze something to the ground.monolingual: to tear down something, usually a building, to ground level. _ The council decided to raze the old city hall to the ground. _ This building is to be razed to the ground.
examples: The council decided to raze the old city hall to the ground.

reach a compromise.monolingual: to achieve a compromise; to negotiate an agreement. _ After many hours of discussion, we finally reached a compromise. _ We were unable to reach a compromise and quit trying.
examples: After many hours of discussion, we finally reached a compromise.

reach a conclusion.monolingual: to complete discussion and decide an issue. _It took three days of talks to reach a conclusion. _ When we reach a conclusion, we will notify you of the results.
examples: It took three days of talks to reach a conclusion.

reach an impasse.monolingual: to progress to the point that a barrier stops further progress. _ When negotiations with management reached an impasse, the union went on strike. _ The discussion reached an impasse and no one was able to propose a compromise.
examples: When negotiations with management reached an impasse, the union went on strike.

reach down.monolingual: to extend downward. _ The stems of the plant reached down almost to the f loor. _The drapes don’t quite reach down to the f loor.
examples: The stems of the plant reached down almost to the f loor.

reach for someone or something.monolingual: to extend one’s grasp to someone or something. _ I reached for my father, but he wasn’t there. _ I reached for a pen, but I only had a pencil.
examples: I reached for my father, but he wasn’t there.

reach out.monolingual: 1. Lit. to extend one’s grasp outward. _ He reached out, but there was no one to take hold of. _I reached out and grabbed onto the first thing I could get hold of.
examples: He reached out, but there was no one to take hold of.

reach out into something.monolingual: to extend one’s grasp out into something, such as the darkness. _Laura reached out into the darkness, looking for the light switch. _ Jane reached out into the unlit room, hoping to find a lamp or even a candle.
examples: Laura reached out into the darkness, looking for the light switch.

reach out to someone.monolingual: 1. Fig. to offer someone a helping hand. _ You reached out to me just when I needed help the most. _ I reach out to other people in trouble because I would want someone to do that for me.
examples: You reached out to me just when I needed help the most.

reach someone.monolingual: 1. Lit. to travel up to or as far as someone. _I ran until I reached her just in time to save her from going over the cliff.
examples: I ran until I reached her just in time to save her from going over the cliff.

reach something down†.monolingual: Inf. to hand something down. _ Please reach the hammer down to me. _ Would you reach down the hammer to Jane?
examples: Please reach the hammer down to me.

reach something up to someone.monolingual: Inf. to hand something up to someone. _ I reached the hammer up to Jack, who was fixing a loose shingle on the roof. _ Please reach this cold drink up to your brother.
examples: I reached the hammer up to Jack, who was fixing a loose shingle on the roof.

reach to something.monolingual: to extend all the way to something. _ Our property reaches to the bank of the river. _The grounds reach all the way to the banks of the river.
examples: Our property reaches to the bank of the river.

reach toward someone or something.monolingual: to aim one’s reach to someone or something. _Sam reached toward Walter and took hold of his shoulder. _ He reached toward the apple but withdrew his hand when he saw it was rotten.
examples: Sam reached toward Walter and took hold of his shoulder.

react against someone or something.monolingual: to respond negatively to someone or something. _Why did she react against me so strongly? _There is no need to react against the plan with such force.
examples: There is no need to react against the plan with such force.

react to someone or something.monolingual: to act in response to someone or something. _ You made some very good points. I would like to take some time to react to you. _ How did Mary react to the news?
examples: You made some very good points.

read about someone or something.monolingual: to read information concerning someone or something. _Did you read about John in the newspaper? _ I read about bonds, and learned a lot about finance.
examples: I read about bonds, and learned a lot about finance.

read between the lines.monolingual: Fig. to infer something (from something else); to try to understand what is meant by something that is not written explicitly or openly. _After listening to what she said, if you read between the lines, you can begin to see what she really means. _ D
examples: After listening to what she said, if you read between the lines, you can begin to see what she really means.

read for something.monolingual: to read, looking especially for something, such as errors, clarity, etc. _ Please read this manuscript for spelling and grammar errors. _ Read this book for entertainment and nothing more.
examples: Please read this manuscript for spelling and grammar errors.

read from something.monolingual: to read [aloud] from something in particular. _ I will now read from a book of poetry that I like very much. _I like that poem very much. What are you reading from?
examples: I will now read from a book of poetry that I like very much.

read it and weep.monolingual: Fig. read the bad news; hear the bad news. _ I’m sorry to bring you the bad news. Read it and weep.
examples: I’m sorry to bring you the bad news.

read on.monolingual: to continue to read. _ Please read on. Don’t stop. _ She read on until she had come to the end of the story.
examples: Please read on.

read one one’s rights.monolingual: to make the required statement of legal rights to a person who has been arrested. _All right, read this guy his rights and book him on a charge of theft. _ You have to read them their rights before questioning them.
examples: All right, read this guy his rights and book him on a charge of theft.

read oneself to sleep.monolingual: to read something in preparation for falling asleep. _ I need a really dull book so I can read myself to sleep. _That’s the kind of book I use to read myself to sleep.
examples: I need a really dull book so I can read myself to sleep.

read someone like a book.monolingual: Fig. to understand someone very well. _ I’ve got John figured out. I can read him like a book. _Of course I understand you. I read you like a book.
examples: I’ve got John figured out.

read someone out of something.monolingual: to expel someone from an organization, such as a political party. _ Because of her statement, they read her out of the party. _ The officers tried to read me out of the society, but they didn’t succeed.
examples: Because of her statement, they read her out of the party.

read someone’s lips.monolingual: to manage to understand speech by watching and interpreting the movements of the speaker’s lips. _ I couldn’t hear her but I could read her lips.
examples: I couldn’t hear her but I could read her lips.

read someone’s mind.monolingual: Fig. to guess what someone is thinking. _You’ll have to tell me what you want. I can’t read your mind, you know. _If I could read your mind, I’d know what you expect of me.
examples: You’ll have to tell me what you want.

read someone the riot act.monolingual: Fig. to give someone a severe scolding. _ The manager read me the riot act for coming in late. _The teacher read the students the riot act for their failure to do their assignments.
examples: The manager read me the riot act for coming in late.

read something in something.monolingual: to read something in particular in a some publication or document. _ I read an interesting article about moose in today’s newspaper. _Did you read that in today’s newspaper?
examples: I read an interesting article about moose in today’s newspaper.

read something into something.monolingual: Fig. to attach or attribute a new or different meaning to something; to presume inferences as one reads something. _ This statement means exactly what it says. Don’t try to read anything else into it. _ Am I reading too much into your comments?
examples: This statement means exactly what it says.

read something off†.monolingual: to read aloud from a list. _ Nick read the list of the names off, and I wasn’t on the list. _Jane read off the names.
examples: Nick read the list of the names off, and I wasn’t on the list.

read something out†.monolingual: to read something aloud. _ Please read it out so everyone can hear you. _Read out the names loudly.
examples: Please read it out so everyone can hear you.

read something over†.monolingual: to read something. _When you have a chance, read this over. _ Also, read over this report.
examples: When you have a chance, read this over.

read something through†.monolingual: to read all of something. _Take this home and read it through. _ Read through this report and see if you can find any errors.
examples: Take this home and read it through.

readjust to someone or something.monolingual: to make a new adjustment to someone or something. _Please make an attempt to readjust your work schedule for the next two weeks. _ I don’t think I can readjust to this climate.
examples: Please make an attempt to readjust your work schedule for the next two weeks.

ready, willing, and able.monolingual: Cliché eager or at least willing [to do something]. _If you need someone to help you move furniture, I’m ready, willing, and able. _Fred is ready, willing, and able to do anything you ask him.
examples: If you need someone to help you move furniture, I’m ready, willing, and able.

the real mccoy.monolingual: an authentic thing or person. _Of course it’s authentic. It’s the real McCoy.
examples: Of course it’s authentic.

the real thing.monolingual: something that is genuine and not an imitation. _ I don’t want frozen yogurt, I want the real thing! Yes, ice cream! _She hates plastic that looks like wood. She wants the real thing.
examples: She hates plastic that looks like wood.

the reality of the situation.monolingual: the truth or actuality of the situation; the way the situation really is. _ The reality of the situation is that we must act right now. _ Let’s face the reality of the situation and go out and get jobs so we can pay our bills.
examples: The reality of the situation is that we must act right now.

realize one’s potential.monolingual: to fulfill one’s potential; to do as well as one possibly can. _ I hope I can get a good education so I can realize my potential.
examples: I hope I can get a good education so I can realize my potential.

realize something from something.monolingual: 1. to perceive something from some kind of evidence. _ I just now realized something from what you’ve been saying. _ Tom realized how wrong he had been from what Mary told him.
examples: I just now realized something from what you’ve been saying.

ream someone out†.monolingual: Sl. to scold someone severely. _ The teacher really reamed him out. _The coach reamed out the whole team.
examples: The teacher really reamed him out.

ream something out†.monolingual: to widen or clean an interior cavity or channel by scraping, grinding, or drilling. _ Ream the opening out so the flow will be faster. _ We had to ream out the pipes so the fuel would f low to the engine.
examples: Ream the opening out so the flow will be faster.

reap something from something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to harvest something from something. _We reaped a fine harvest from our cornfields this year. _They will reap nothing from their flooded fields.
examples: We reaped a fine harvest from our cornfields this year.

reappoint someone as something.monolingual: to select or appoint someone to serve again in the same office. _ Are they going to reappoint Alan as the chairman again? _Alan was reappointed as the head of the committee.
examples: Alan was reappointed as the head of the committee.

rear back.monolingual: 1. Lit. [for a horse] to pull back and up onto its hind legs in an effort to move backwards rapidly or throw a rider. _ The animal reared back in terror. _ The horse reared back and almost threw its rider.
examples: The animal reared back in terror.

rear its ugly head.monolingual: Fig. [for something unpleasant] to appear or become obvious after lying hidden. _ Jealousy reared its ugly head and destroyed their marriage. _ The question of money always rears its ugly head in matters of business.
examples: Jealousy reared its ugly head and destroyed their marriage.

rear up.monolingual: 1. Lit. [for a horse] to lean back on its hind legs and raise its front legs, assuming a threatening posture or avoiding something on the ground such as a snake. _ The horse reared up suddenly, throwing the rider onto the ground. _ When the horse rea
examples: The horse reared up suddenly, throwing the rider onto the ground.

reason against something.monolingual: to argue against something, using reason. _ I can hardly be expected to reason against a silly argument like that! _ I reasoned against it, but they paid no attention to me.
examples: I reasoned against it, but they paid no attention to me.

reason something out†.monolingual: to figure something out; to plan a reasonable course of action. _ Now let’s be calm and try to reason this out. _ Let us reason out our difficulties.
examples: Now let’s be calm and try to reason this out.

reason with someone.monolingual: to discuss something with someone, seeking a reasonable solution to a problem. _ Try to reason with Jill. If she won’t listen, forget her. _ You cannot reason with someone who is so narrow-minded.
examples: Try to reason with Jill.

reassign someone to something.monolingual: to change someone’s assignment to something else. _I will reassign Jill to a different department. _ I was reassigned to the accounting department.
examples: I will reassign Jill to a different department.

reassure someone about something.monolingual: to give someone confidence about something. _ Nancy reassured Betty about her promotion. _Betty was reassured about her promotion.
examples: Nancy reassured Betty about her promotion.

reassure someone of something.monolingual: to promise or guarantee someone something. _ Kelly reassured her friend of her support in the election. _ Please reassure Tom of our continued support.
examples: Kelly reassured her friend of her support in the election.

rebel against someone or something.monolingual: to resist and revolt against someone or something. _Barbara rebelled against the teachers at the school. _Most young people have to rebel against authority for a while.
examples: Barbara rebelled against the teachers at the school.

rebel at someone or something.monolingual: to resist and defy someone or something. _ It is natural for teenagers to rebel at their parents. _ I feel as if I have to rebel at all these rules.
examples: It is natural for teenagers to rebel at their parents.

rebound from something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to bounce back from something. _ The ball rebounded from the wall and hit Randy hard on the elbow. _When the ball rebounded from the backboard, it bounced onto the court and Tom tripped on it.
examples: The ball rebounded from the wall and hit Randy hard on the elbow.

rebuke someone for something.monolingual: to reprimand someone for something. _ There is no need to rebuke me for a simple mistake like that. _Sally was rebuked for overspending her budget.
examples: There is no need to rebuke me for a simple mistake like that.

recall someone from something.monolingual: to call someone back from something or some place. _ The president recalled our ambassador from the war-torn country. _ I was recalled from retirement to help out at the office.
examples: The president recalled our ambassador from the war-torn country.

recall something to mind.monolingual: to cause [someone] to remember something. _ The events of the day recall similar days in the past to mind. _This book recalls a similar book published some years ago to mind.
examples: The events of the day recall similar days in the past to mind.

recall something to someone.monolingual: to bring something to the mind of someone. _ Your comments recall another event to me—something that happened years ago. _ What you just said recalled an old saying to me.
examples: Your comments recall another event to me—something that happened years ago.

recast something in something.monolingual: to rebuild or redevelop something in a different form. _She recast the sentence in the negative, hoping to make it less blunt. _ I will recast my request in different language.
examples: She recast the sentence in the negative, hoping to make it less blunt.

recede from something.monolingual: to pull back from something. _ The river receded from its banks during the dry season. _ I think that my hair is receding from my forehead.
examples: The river receded from its banks during the dry season.

receive someone into something.monolingual: to welcome someone into something, some place, or some organization. _ Everyone received the new member into the club with eager congratulations. _ We received them into our homes and fed them well.
examples: Everyone received the new member into the club with eager congratulations.

receive someone or something back.monolingual: to get someone or something back. _Martha received her husband back after his escapade. _ I sent a letter off with the wrong postage and received it back two weeks later.
examples: Martha received her husband back after his escapade.

receive something from some place.monolingual: to get and accept something from some place. _ I just received a letter from Budapest! _ Mary received a package from Japan.
examples: Mary received a package from Japan.

receive something from someone.monolingual: to get and accept something from someone. _ Tony received a sweater from his grandfather for his birthday. _ Who did you receive this from?
examples: Tony received a sweater from his grandfather for his birthday.

reckon with someone or something.monolingual: to deal with someone or something; to cope with someone or something. _ I have to reckon with the troublesome Mr. Johnson this afternoon. _Mary knew just exactly how she had to reckon with the bill collector.
examples: I have to reckon with the troublesome Mr.

reckon without someone.monolingual: to fail to think about someone. _ He thought he’d get away with his crime, but he reckoned without the FBI agents. _He had thought he was gone for sure, but he had reckoned without the paramedics.
examples: He thought he’d get away with his crime, but he reckoned without the FBI agents.

recoil from someone or something.monolingual: to draw back from someone or something. _I recoiled from Sally when she told me what she had done. _ I recoiled from the horror and slammed the door.
examples: I recoiled from Sally when she told me what she had done.

recommend someone as something.monolingual: to suggest someone as something. _ Could you recommend Frank as a good carpenter? _I can recommend Jane Smith as a good artist.
examples: I can recommend Jane Smith as a good artist.

recommend someone for something.monolingual: to suggest someone for something. _ I would be very glad to recommend you for promotion. _ She recommended herself as the best choice.
examples: I would be very glad to recommend you for promotion.

recompense someone for something.monolingual: to (re)pay someone for something. _ I am required to recompense Mrs. Wilson for her broken window. _ Can I recompense you for your expenses?
examples: I am required to recompense Mrs.

reconcile oneself to something.monolingual: to grow to feel comfortable with an undesirable or challenging situation. _ John reconciled himself to living alone. _ Anne reconciled herself to having to wear glasses.
examples: John reconciled himself to living alone.

reconcile something with something.monolingual: to bring something into harmony, accord, or balance with something. _ The accountants were not able to reconcile the expense claims with the receipts that had been turned in. _ I can’t reconcile your story with those of the other witnesses.
examples: The accountants were not able to reconcile the expense claims with the receipts that had been turned in.

reconstruct something from something.monolingual: 1. to rebuild something from something. _I was not able to reconstruct the puzzle from the pieces that were left on the f loor. _Can you reconstruct the damaged part of the house from these materials?
examples: I was not able to reconstruct the puzzle from the pieces that were left on the f loor.

record something from something.monolingual: to make an audio or video recording of something from some source. _ Listen to this. I recorded it from a radio broadcast. _ From what TV show did you record this?
examples: Listen to this.

record something in something.monolingual: to enter a record of something into something. _I will record your appointment in my notebook. _ Jane recorded the memo in her computer.
examples: I will record your appointment in my notebook.

record something on something.monolingual: to make a record of something on the surface of something. _ Nancy recorded the appointment on the calendar that served as a blotter on the top of her desk. _ Please record this on your calendar.
examples: Nancy recorded the appointment on the calendar that served as a blotter on the top of her desk.

recount something to someone.monolingual: to tell something to someone; to narrate a series of events, in order. _ Carl recounted the events of the day to his wife. _ The strange events were recounted by a number of people.
examples: Carl recounted the events of the day to his wife.

recover from someone or something.monolingual: to get over an experience with someone or something. _ My great-uncle just left, and it will take a day or two to recover from him. _ I hope I recover from his visit soon.
examples: My great-uncle just left, and it will take a day or two to recover from him.

recover from something.monolingual: to recuperate from a disease. _ I hope I recover from this cough soon. _She recovered from her cold soon enough to go on the trip.
examples: I hope I recover from this cough soon.

recruit someone for something.monolingual: to seek and engage someone for something. _Harry had to recruit a few people for the new jobs that opened up. _We recruited three more people for the project.
examples: Harry had to recruit a few people for the new jobs that opened up.

recruit someone from something.monolingual: to convince someone to leave something and join one’s own group. _ Phyllis recruited a new work team from the company she used to work for. _ We recruited a number of people from private industry.
examples: Phyllis recruited a new work team from the company she used to work for.

recruit someone into something.monolingual: to seek out and induct someone into something. _ The recruitment office tried to recruit ten people a week into the army. _ The army recruited almost no one during the month of December.
examples: The recruitment office tried to recruit ten people a week into the army.

recuperate from something.monolingual: to recover from something; to be cured or to heal after something. _ I hope that you recuperate from your illness soon. _ Has she recuperated from her surgery yet?
examples: I hope that you recuperate from your illness soon.

a red herring.monolingual: a piece of information or suggestion introduced to draw attention away from the real facts of a situation. (A red herring is a type of strong-smelling smoked fish that was once drawn across the trail of a scent to mislead hunting dogs and put them of
examples: The detectives were following a red herring, but they’re on the right track now.

red in the face.monolingual: Fig. embarrassed. _ After we found Ann hiding in the closet, she became red in the face. _ The speaker kept making errors and became red in the face.
examples: After we found Ann hiding in the closet, she became red in the face.

red ink.monolingual: Fig. debt; indebtedness as shown in red ink on a financial statement. _ There is too much red ink in my financial statement. _ Too much red ink and the company will collapse.
examples: There is too much red ink in my financial statement.

red tape.monolingual: Fig. over-strict attention to the wording and details of rules and regulations, especially by government workers. (From the color of the tape used by government departments in England to tie up bundles of documents.) _Because of red tape, Frank took
examples: Because of red tape, Frank took weeks to get a visa.

*the red-carpet treatment.monolingual: Fig. very special treatment; royal treatment. (*Typically: get ~; have ~; give someone ~.) _ I love to go to fancy stores where I get the red-carpet treatment. _ The queen expects to get the redcarpet treatment wherever she goes.
examples: I love to go to fancy stores where I get the red-carpet treatment.

a red-letter day.monolingual: Fig. an important or significant day. (From the practice of printing holidays in red on the calendar.) _ Today was a red-letter day in our history. _ It was a red-letter day for our club.
examples: Today was a red-letter day in our history.

redound on someone.monolingual: to have an effect on someone. _The hot weather has redounded on all of us in a bad way. _The problems created by your mistake have redounded on the entire company.
examples: The hot weather has redounded on all of us in a bad way.

reduce someone to silence.monolingual: to cause someone to be silent. _The rebuke reduced him to silence—at last. _Mary was reduced to silence by Jane’s comments.
examples: The rebuke reduced him to silence—at last.

reduce someone to tears.monolingual: to cause a person to cry through insults, frustration, and belittling. _ He scolded her so much that she was reduced to tears by the end of the meeting.
examples: He scolded her so much that she was reduced to tears by the end of the meeting.

reduce something by something.monolingual: to diminish something by a certain amount. _I have to reduce your allowance by two dollars per week until you pay me back for the broken window. _ I will reduce the bill by a few dollars.
examples: I have to reduce your allowance by two dollars per week until you pay me back for the broken window.

reduced to doing something.monolingual: brought into a certain humble condition or state. _The poor man was reduced to begging for food.
examples: The poor man was reduced to begging for food.

reef a sail in†.monolingual: to reduce the area of a ship’s sail, by folding the sail. _The first mate ordered the sailors to reef the sails in. _ They had to reef in the sails.
examples: The first mate ordered the sailors to reef the sails in.

reek of something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to have the stench or smell of something. _ This whole house reeks of onions! What did you cook? _ She reeks of a very strong perfume. She must have spilled it on herself.
examples: She reeks of a very strong perfume.

reek with something.monolingual: to stink with some smell. _This place reeks with some horrible odor. _ Jane reeks with too much perfume.
examples: This place reeks with some horrible odor.

reel something in†.monolingual: to bring in something, such as a fish, by winding up the line on a reel. _With great effort, she reeled the huge fish in. _ Hurry and reel in the fish!
examples: With great effort, she reeled the huge fish in.

reel under something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to stagger under the weight of something. _Tony reeled under the weight of the books. _ She knew she would reel under the heavy load.
examples: Tony reeled under the weight of the books.

refer to someone or something.monolingual: to mention someone or something. _Are you referring to me when you speak about a kind and helpful person? _ I was referring to the personnel department.
examples: I was referring to the personnel department.

refill a prescription.monolingual: sell a second or subsequent set of doses of a medicine upon a doctor’s orders. _ The pharmacy refused to refill my prescription because it has expired. _ If you want the drugstore to refill your prescription, just give them the prescription number ov
examples: The pharmacy refused to refill my prescription because it has expired.

reflected in something.monolingual: 1. Lit. [of something] mirrored in something, such as a mirror, water, ice, etc. _ His image was ref lected in the mirror, giving him a good view of his sunburn. _ When the hermit’s image was ref lected in the pool, he was amazed.
examples: His image was ref lected in the mirror, giving him a good view of his sunburn.

refrain from something.monolingual: to hold back from doing something; to choose not to do something as planned. _I wish you would refrain from shouting. _Please refrain from hollering.
examples: I wish you would refrain from shouting.

refresh someone with something.monolingual: to renew or revive someone with something. _Here, let me refresh you with a cool glass of lemonade. _ After the game, Wally will probably refresh himself with a bottle of iced tea.
examples: Here, let me refresh you with a cool glass of lemonade.

refresh something with something.monolingual: to restore or brighten up something. _ I think we can refresh this drab old room with a coat of fresh paint. _ The old house was refreshed with new siding and some landscaping.
examples: I think we can refresh this drab old room with a coat of fresh paint.

refund something to someone.monolingual: to return payment for something to someone. _ I insist that you refund the money to me at once. _ Her money was refunded to her by the store as soon as she asked for it.
examples: I insist that you refund the money to me at once.

refuse something to someone.monolingual: to deny someone permission to receive or use something. _ You wouldn’t refuse water to me, would you? _ Nothing at all was refused to the new employee.
examples: Nothing at all was refused to the new employee.

refuse to do something.monolingual: to reject doing something; to reject a request to do something. _I absolutely refuse to go there! _ We all refused to break the law.
examples: We all refused to break the law.

regain one’s composure.monolingual: Cliché to become calm and composed after being angry or agitated. _ I found it difficult to regain my composure after the argument. _ Here, sit down and relax so that you can regain your composure.
examples: I found it difficult to regain my composure after the argument.

regain one’s feet.monolingual: 1. Lit. to stand up again after falling or stumbling. _I fell on the ice and almost couldn’t regain my feet. _ I helped my uncle regain his feet as he tried to get up from the f loor.
examples: I fell on the ice and almost couldn’t regain my feet.

regale someone with something.monolingual: to present a great deal of something, such as lavish entertainment or fine food, to someone. _ They regaled their guests with food and music well into the night. _The committee was regaled with tales of wrongdoing by the government.
examples: They regaled their guests with food and music well into the night.

regardless of something.monolingual: without considering something; at any rate; whatever is done; whatever option is chosen. _ Regardless of what you say, I’m still going to the club tonight. _ I still have to pay the bill, regardless of the facts.
examples: Regardless of what you say, I’m still going to the club tonight.

register for something.monolingual: to sign up to participate in something. _Have you registered for the class yet? _She is registered for the same classes as I am.
examples: She is registered for the same classes as I am.

register in something.monolingual: to enter one’s name on a list for something; to sign oneself up to belong to something. _ Are you going to register in the pie-eating contest? _We registered in the drawing for a new car.
examples: We registered in the drawing for a new car.

register on something.monolingual: [for an effect] to show on something, such as someone’s face. _Recognition registered on her face when she saw the photograph of Walter. _The total of the votes registered on the large scoreboard at the front of the hall.
examples: Recognition registered on her face when she saw the photograph of Walter.

register someone as something.monolingual: to record someone’s name on a list of a category of people. _I will register you as an independent voter. _ I am registered as a qualified financial advisor.
examples: I will register you as an independent voter.

register someone for something.monolingual: to sign someone up to participate in something. _ Would you please register me for the workshop when you sign up? _ Excuse me. I have to go register myself for the contest.
examples: Excuse me. I have to go register myself for the contest.

register someone in something.monolingual: 1. to enter someone’s name on a list in something. _ I will register you in the competition.
examples: I will register you in the competition.

register with someone.monolingual: 1. Lit. to sign up with someone. _ You will have to register with the lady at the front desk. _ I registered with the attendant when I came in.
examples: You will have to register with the lady at the front desk.

regress to something.monolingual: to go back to an earlier, probably simpler, state; to go back to a more primitive state. _ Bob claimed that Gerald’s behavior was regressing to that of a three-year-old. _ I tend to regress to my college ways when I am out with the guys.
examples: Bob claimed that Gerald’s behavior was regressing to that of a three-year-old.

*regular as clockwork.monolingual: Cliché very regular; completely predictable. (*Also: as ~.) _George goes down to the bus stop at 7:45 every morning, as regular as clockwork. _ You can always depend on Nancy to complain about the office for fifteen minutes every afternoon, regular a
examples: George goes down to the bus stop at 7:45 every morning, as regular as clockwork.

a regular fixture.monolingual: someone who is found so frequently in a place as to be considered a fixture of, or part of the place. _ The manager attached himself to the luncheon club and became a regular fixture there.
examples: The manager attached himself to the luncheon club and became a regular fixture there.

a regular guy.monolingual: a normal and dependable guy. _ Don’t worry about Tom. He’s a regular guy. He won’t give you any trouble.
examples: Don’t worry about Tom.

rehearse for something.monolingual: to practice for something. _ We will rehearse for the graduation exercises on Saturday morning. _ We rehearsed for the play all weekend.
examples: We will rehearse for the graduation exercises on Saturday morning.

reign over someone or something.monolingual: to rule over someone or something. _ The king reigned over his subjects for over thirty years. _The queen reigned over the country for a long time.
examples: The king reigned over his subjects for over thirty years.

reimburse someone for something.monolingual: to repay someone for making a purchase, such as a business expense. _ I will reimburse you for whatever it cost you. _ The treasurer reimbursed himself for his expenses.
examples: I will reimburse you for whatever it cost you.

reimburse something to someone.monolingual: to repay money to someone, such as a business expense. _ I will reimburse the money to you. Don’t worry. _The full cost was reimbursed to me.
examples: I will reimburse the money to you.

rein someone or something in†.monolingual: to bring someone or something under control; to slow down someone or something. _ Fred is getting out of hand. The boss undertook to rein him in a bit. _ The boss is trying to rein in Jane’s enthusiasm.
examples: Fred is getting out of hand.

rein something up†.monolingual: to bring something, usually a horse, to a stop. _She reined her horse up and stopped for a chat. _ Rein up your horse and stop for a while.
examples: She reined her horse up and stopped for a chat.

rein up.monolingual: [for a horse rider] to stop. _The equestrian reined up and dismounted. _We all reined up and waited for the cars to pass by.
examples: The equestrian reined up and dismounted.

reinstate someone as something.monolingual: to put someone back as a certain officeholder. _The city council agreed to reinstate Mr. Wilson as alderman. _Fred was reinstated as the court clerk.
examples: The city council agreed to reinstate Mr.

reinstate someone in something.monolingual: to put someone back into a certain office or position. _If you will pay your dues, we will reinstate you in the organization. _Fred was reinstated in office.
examples: If you will pay your dues, we will reinstate you in the organization.

reinvent the wheel.monolingual: Fig. to make unnecessary or redundant preparations. _ You don’t need to reinvent the wheel. Read up on what others have done. _ I don’t have to reinvent the wheel, but I will be cautious before I act.
examples: You don’t need to reinvent the wheel.

reissue something to someone.monolingual: to release or distribute to someone something that has been distributed before. _I plan to reissue the check to you next week. _The check was reissued to Mary the very next day.
examples: I plan to reissue the check to you next week.

rejoice at something.monolingual: to celebrate or revel about something. _Everyone rejoiced at the lucky events that had saved them. _ We all rejoiced at the outcome of the election.
examples: Everyone rejoiced at the lucky events that had saved them.

rejoice in someone or something.monolingual: to take great joy at someone or something. _ I am in love and I rejoice in my beloved! _ Roger rejoices in a good night’s sleep.
examples: Roger rejoices in a good night’s sleep.

rejoice over something.monolingual: to celebrate because of something. _ Everyone rejoiced over their good fortune. _ What happened to us next was nothing to rejoice over.
examples: Everyone rejoiced over their good fortune.

relapse into something.monolingual: to experience a return to a worse condition. _Valerie relapsed into a coma in the afternoon. _ Mary relapsed into her depression after a brief period of normalcy.
examples: Valerie relapsed into a coma in the afternoon.

relate something to someone.monolingual: to tell something to someone; to narrate something to someone. _ Very slowly, she related the events of the past week to her parents. _ I have an interesting story to relate to you.
examples: Very slowly, she related the events of the past week to her parents.

relate something to something.monolingual: to associate something to something. _I relate this particular problem to the failure of the company to provide proper training. _ This point is related to what I just told you.
examples: I relate this particular problem to the failure of the company to provide proper training.

relate to someone or something.monolingual: to understand, accept, or feel kinship with someone or something. _ He relates to people well. _ I really don’t relate to your thinking at all.
examples: He relates to people well.

*related to someone.monolingual: connected through blood kinship or through marriage to someone. (*Typically: be ~; become ~.) _ I wonder if he is related to you, because he looks a little like you. _ I am not related to anyone here.
examples: I wonder if he is related to you, because he looks a little like you.

relative to someone or something.monolingual: 1. concerning someone or something. _ I have something to say relative to Bill. _ Do you have any information relative to the situation in South America?
examples: I have something to say relative to Bill.

relax into something.monolingual: 1. to sit or lie down in something, relaxing. _I want to go home and relax into my easy chair. _ I relaxed into the reclining chair and was asleep in a few moments.
examples: I want to go home and relax into my easy chair.

relay something to someone.monolingual: to pass something on to someone. _ Can you relay this to Frank, who is way down the line? _ The message was relayed to Frank, who was at the end of the line.
examples: The message was relayed to Frank, who was at the end of the line.

release someone to someone.monolingual: to discharge or distribute someone to someone. _ The judge released the defendant to his mother. _Don was released by the police to his father, who was more than a little bit angry.
examples: The judge released the defendant to his mother.

reliance on someone or something.monolingual: trust and dependence on someone or something. _ John’s reliance on his family is holding him back. _ Reliance on sleeping pills is dangerous.
examples: John’s reliance on his family is holding him back.

relieve one of one’s duties.monolingual: Euph. to fire someone; to dismiss someone from employment. _ I am afraid I must relieve you of your duties. _ After the scandal, she was relieved of her duties at the embassy.
examples: I am afraid I must relieve you of your duties.

relieve oneself.monolingual: Euph. to urinate or defecate. _ He stopped by the side of the road to relieve himself. _She needed badly to relieve herself, but there was no bathroom in sight.
examples: He stopped by the side of the road to relieve himself.

relieve someone of something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to unburden someone of something. _Here, let me relieve you of that heavy box. _ At last, he could relieve himself of the problem.
examples: Here, let me relieve you of that heavy box.

religious about doing something.monolingual: Fig. strict about something; conscientious about something. _ Bob is religious about paying his bills on time. _ Max tries to be religious about being polite to everyone.
examples: Bob is religious about paying his bills on time.

relinquish something over someone.monolingual: to release the hold on or control of someone. _ She refused to relinquish control over the operations of the front office. _Mary was ordered to relinquish her hold over the children for a month each year.
examples: She refused to relinquish control over the operations of the front office.

reluctant to do something.monolingual: unwilling to do something; not wanting to do something. _David was reluctant to admit his mistakes. _ Although reluctant to appear in court, the witness was ordered to by subpoena.
examples: David was reluctant to admit his mistakes.

remain at some place.monolingual: to stay at some place; to stay behind at some place. _ I will remain at the office until supper time. _ Please remain at home until I call you.
examples: I will remain at the office until supper time.

remain behind.monolingual: to stay at a place even when others have left. _Can’t I go too? Do I have to remain behind? _I will remain behind for a day or two.
examples: I will remain behind for a day or two.

remain down.monolingual: to stay down; to keep down. _I asked them to remain down until the shooting stopped. _Please remain down with me so no one will see us.
examples: I asked them to remain down until the shooting stopped.

remain together.monolingual: to stay close together; to stay in association. _ We will have to remain together while we are on this tour. It is very easy to get lost in this town. _ The two boys remained together throughout college.
examples: We will have to remain together while we are on this tour.

remain under something.monolingual: to continue to stay beneath the surface of something. _Please remain under the umbrella so you don’t get wet. _ A lot of people decided to leave the shelter, but I remained under it.
examples: Please remain under the umbrella so you don’t get wet.

remain up.monolingual: to stay awake and out of bed. _ I remained up throughout most of the night. _ I cannot remain up much longer.
examples: I remained up throughout most of the night.

remember me to someone..monolingual: Please carry my good wishes to someone. (The someone can be a person’s name or a pronoun.) _ Tom: My brother says hello. Bill: Oh, good. Please remember me to him. Tom: I will. _Fred: Bye. John: Good-bye, Fred. Remember me to your Uncle Tom.
examples: Tom: My brother says hello.

remember someone as something.monolingual: to recall someone as being a particular type of person. _ I remember Terri as a rather cheerful girl, always willing to help out. _William will be remembered as a grouchy person.
examples: I remember Terri as a rather cheerful girl, always willing to help out.

remember someone in one’s will.monolingual: to bequeath something to someone in one’s will. _My uncle always said he would remember me in his will. _ He failed to remember me in his will.
examples: My uncle always said he would remember me in his will.

remember someone to someone.monolingual: to carry the greetings of someone to someone else. _ Please remember all of us to your uncle. _ I will remember you to my brother, who asks of you often.
examples: Please remember all of us to your uncle.

reminisce about someone or something.monolingual: to think about one’s memories of someone or something; to discuss or share memories of someone or something. _ They were reminiscing about their old friends. _ The old men sat and reminisced about the good old days.
examples: They were reminiscing about their old friends.

reminisce with someone.monolingual: to share memories with someone. _ I love to reminisce with my sister about old times. _Todd was reminiscing with Alice about the good old days.
examples: I love to reminisce with my sister about old times.

reminiscent of someone or something.monolingual: reminding someone about someone or something; seeming like or suggesting someone or something. _ This fragrance is reminiscent of fresh f lowers. _ Jane’s dress seems reminiscent of the style worn in the 1920s.
examples: This fragrance is reminiscent of fresh f lowers.

remove someone from something.monolingual: to take someone out of an office or position. _ The county board removed the sheriff from office. _ She removed herself from office voluntarily.
examples: The county board removed the sheriff from office.

remunerate someone for something.monolingual: 1. to pay someone for something. _ Of course, I will remunerate you for your time. _ She was promptly remunerated for the hours she spent working on the project.
examples: Of course, I will remunerate you for your time.

rend something into something.monolingual: to rip or tear something into something. (The past tense and past participle are rent.) _ The tailor rent the garment into shreds in his anger. _ The garment was rent into bits and pieces by the machine.
examples: The tailor rent the garment into shreds in his anger.

render something down†.monolingual: 1. Lit. to cook the fat out of something. _ Polly rendered the chicken fat down to a bit of golden grease that she would use in cooking a special dish. _Jane rendered down the fat for use later. _The cook rendered it down.
examples: Polly rendered the chicken fat down to a bit of golden grease that she would use in cooking a special dish.

renege on something.monolingual: to go back on one’s promise or commitment. _ I am mad at you because you reneged on your promise! _ I did not renege on what I promised.
examples: I did not renege on what I promised.

renounce someone for something.monolingual: to repudiate someone for doing something. _She renounced her brother for his political orientation. _Jane was renounced for her illegal activities.
examples: She renounced her brother for his political orientation.

rent something from someone.monolingual: to pay someone for the use of something. _ We rented a small car from one of the rental agencies. _They rented a house from a local realtor.
examples: We rented a small car from one of the rental agencies.

repair to some place.monolingual: to move oneself to some place. _ I will repair to my room until the crisis is over. _She repaired to a safe place for the duration of the storm.
examples: I will repair to my room until the crisis is over.

repatriate someone to some place.monolingual: to restore one to one’s country of origin. _ He asked that they repatriate him to the land of his birth. _ She was repatriated to her homeland.
examples: He asked that they repatriate him to the land of his birth.

repay someone by something.monolingual: to recompense someone by doing something; to settle a debt with someone by doing something. _I will repay you by cutting your lawn free for a year. How’s that? _Can I repay you by taking you to dinner?
examples: I will repay you by cutting your lawn free for a year.

repay someone for something.monolingual: to remunerate someone for doing something. _I refused to repay him for his excessive expenses. _ She was repaid for her kindness many times over.
examples: I refused to repay him for his excessive expenses.

repay someone with something.monolingual: to remunerate someone with something. _ The farmer’s wife repaid the plumbers with fresh eggs and cream. _We were repaid with fresh eggs from the farm.
examples: The farmer’s wife repaid the plumbers with fresh eggs and cream.

repel someone from something.monolingual: to push someone back from something; to fight someone off from something. _ The army repelled the attackers from the entrance to the city. _ The attacking army was repelled from the city.
examples: The army repelled the attackers from the entrance to the city.

replenish something with something.monolingual: to rebuild the supply of something with more of it. _I will replenish the checking account with more money at the end of the month. _ Can I replenish your glass with more iced tea?
examples: I will replenish the checking account with more money at the end of the month.

reply to someone or something.monolingual: to give a response to someone or something. _ I replied to her already. There is no reason to do it again. _ I will reply to her letter as soon as I can.
examples: I replied to her already.

report about someone or something.monolingual: to deliver information about someone or something. _ Isn’t it time to report about Frank and how well he is doing? _ I want to report about the accident.
examples: I want to report about the accident.

report for something.monolingual: to present oneself for something. _ Please report for duty on Monday morning at eight o’clock sharp. _ I can’t report for my examination at the time we agreed upon.
examples: Please report for duty on Monday morning at eight o’clock sharp.

report in.monolingual: to present oneself; to make one’s presence known. _ Please report in when you get back in town. _ He reported in and his name was taken off the absentee list.
examples: Please report in when you get back in town.

report in sick.monolingual: to call one’s office to say that one will not come to work because one is sick; to show up for work ill. _ I don’t feel well today. I will report in sick. _ The phone was busy, so I reported in sick by e-mail.
examples: I don’t feel well today.

report something to someone.monolingual: to present a body of information to someone. _Please report the results to the supervisor. _ The event was reported to the proper person.
examples: Please report the results to the supervisor.

report to someone or something.monolingual: 1. to present oneself to someone or an office. _ You must report to me for duty at noon. _ They told me to report to this office at this time.
examples: You must report to me for duty at noon.

repose in something.monolingual: 1. to lie stretched out in something, such as a bed. _ I think I would like to repose in my own bed for an hour or two before I begin my journey. _ Tom reposed in a comfortable chair for the rest of the evening.
examples: I think I would like to repose in my own bed for an hour or two before I begin my journey.

represent someone in something.monolingual: to act as one’s advocate or agent in business or legal proceedings. _ My lawyer represented me in court. _ His attorney will represent him in all his dealings with the publishing company.
examples: My lawyer represented me in court.

represent something to someone.monolingual: 1. to exemplify something to someone. _ What does this behavior represent to you? _ This represents a lapse in manners to me.
examples: This represents a lapse in manners to me.

reprimand someone for something.monolingual: to scold someone for something; to admonish someone for something. _There is no need to reprimand me for a simple accident! _ Mary was reprimanded for being late.
examples: Mary was reprimanded for being late.

reproach someone for something.monolingual: to rebuke or censure someone for something. _ She reproached Jerry for gambling away all their money. _ She reproached herself mercilessly for her failure.
examples: She reproached Jerry for gambling away all their money.

reproach someone with something.monolingual: to rebuke someone with reference to something. _ I wish you wouldn’t continue to reproach me with things that happened long ago. _ She was reproached with something out of the past.
examples: I wish you wouldn’t continue to reproach me with things that happened long ago.

reproduce something from something.monolingual: to make a copy of something from something else. _ I think we can reproduce the picture from the copy that you have there. We don’t need the negative. _ Can you reproduce a good copy from this old print?
examples: I think we can reproduce the picture from the copy that you have there.

reprove someone for something.monolingual: to criticize or censure someone for something. _ The boss reproved all the employees for their use of the telephones for personal calls. _ We were all reproved for being late too often.
examples: The boss reproved all the employees for their use of the telephones for personal calls.

reputed to.monolingual: thought to do, be, or have someone or something. _My boss is reputed to have cancer. _My neighbor was reputed to have been a spy during the war.
examples: My boss is reputed to have cancer.

request someone to do something.monolingual: to ask someone to do something. _ I am going to request you to turn your radio down. _Mary was requested to arrive a few minutes early.
examples: I am going to request you to turn your radio down.

request something from someone.monolingual: to call for something from someone. _ I will request an explanation from the employee in question. _ A full report was requested from each person present.
examples: I will request an explanation from the employee in question.

request something of someone.monolingual: to call for someone to give or do something. _I have to request a favor of you. _Can I request anything more of him?
examples: I have to request a favor of you.

require something from someone.monolingual: to demand something from someone. _ The telephone company required a deposit from John and Martha before they would install a telephone. _ They required some help from us.
examples: The telephone company required a deposit from John and Martha before they would install a telephone.

require something of someone.monolingual: to expect or demand someone to give or do something. _ I require absolute loyalty of my employees. _ What is required of me in this job?
examples: I require absolute loyalty of my employees.

research into someone or something.monolingual: to study about someone or something thoroughly. _ I decided that I would research into Queen Elizabeth. _ We researched into the period in which she lived.
examples: I decided that I would research into Queen Elizabeth.

reside in some place.monolingual: to dwell in some place. _ I reside in a small apartment in the center of town. _ The Wilsons resided in a large house on a hill.
examples: I reside in a small apartment in the center of town.

reside in someone or something.monolingual: to be a property or characteristic of someone or something. _ I never knew such anger could reside in such a calm person. _ The finest acoustics that can be found in the world reside in this hall.
examples: I never knew such anger could reside in such a calm person.

resign from something.monolingual: to make a written statement that removes one from an office or position of employment. _Andy resigned from the fraternity. _I will not resign from my job. You will have to fire me.
examples: Andy resigned from the fraternity.

resign oneself to something.monolingual: to accept something reluctantly. _ I finally resigned myself to going to Mexico even though I didn’t want to. _ Mary resigned herself to her fate.
examples: I finally resigned myself to going to Mexico even though I didn’t want to.

resonate with someone.monolingual: Fig. [for an idea, issue, or concept] to appeal to someone or cause someone to relate to it. _ The concept of wearing worn-looking clothing seems to resonate with young people. _ Your notion just doesn’t resonate with the public in general.
examples: The concept of wearing worn-looking clothing seems to resonate with young people.

resort to something.monolingual: to turn to something that is not the first choice. _I hope they don’t resort to a lawsuit to accomplish their goals. _She will resort to anything to get her way.
examples: I hope they don’t resort to a lawsuit to accomplish their goals.

resound with something.monolingual: [for something, such as the air or a place] to be filled with sound or sounds. _ The hall resounded with the sounds of the orchestra. _ The house resounded with the laughter of children.
examples: The hall resounded with the sounds of the orchestra.

respect someone as something.monolingual: to admire someone as something. _ I respect you as a friend and supervisor. _ We respected them all as colleagues and coworkers.
examples: I respect you as a friend and supervisor.

respect someone for something.monolingual: to admire someone for something. _ I really respect George for his courage. _ Mary respected the company for its fine products.
examples: I really respect George for his courage.

respond to someone or something.monolingual: 1. to answer someone or something. _ Would you please respond to me? _ When are you going to respond to my letter?
examples: When are you going to respond to my letter? 2.

the responsible party.monolingual: the person or organization responsible or liable for something. _ I intend to find the responsible party and get some answers to my questions. _ Mary sued the responsible party in the car crash.
examples: I intend to find the responsible party and get some answers to my questions.

rest against someone or something.monolingual: to lean against someone or something; to take a rest period positioned against someone or something. _ The child rested against his father until it was time to board the train. _ A fishing pole rested against the side of the garage, ready to go to wo
examples: The child rested against his father until it was time to board the train.

rest assured.monolingual: to be assured; to be certain. _ Rest assured that you’ll receive the best of care. _Please rest assured that we will do everything possible to help.
examples: Rest assured that you’ll receive the best of care.

rest from something.monolingual: to take it easy and recover from something. _ I need to take a few minutes and rest from all that exertion. _When you have rested from your running, please come in here and help me.
examples: I need to take a few minutes and rest from all that exertion.

rest in peace.monolingual: to lie dead peacefully for eternity. (A solemn entreaty used in funeral prayers, eulogies, etc.) _ We prayed that the deceased would rest in peace. _ The bodies of the soldiers will rest in peace.
examples: We prayed that the deceased would rest in peace.

rest in something.monolingual: 1. to be comfortable in something, such as a chair or a bed. _ I rested in the chair for a while and then got up and made supper. _ I will rest in bed until I feel better.
examples: I rested in the chair for a while and then got up and made supper.

the rest is gravy..monolingual: Fig. Any additional money received is just an easily acquired bonus. _There is some cost involved in buying the raw materials, and the cost of manufacturing is negligible. When we pay off the costs, the rest is gravy.
examples: There is some cost involved in buying the raw materials, and the cost of manufacturing is negligible.

the rest is history..monolingual: Fig. Everyone knows the rest of the story that I am referring to. _ Bill: Then they arrested all the officers of the corporation, and the rest is history. _Bob: Hey, what happened between you and Sue? Bill: Finally we realized that we could never get
examples: Bill: Then they arrested all the officers of the corporation, and the rest is history.

rest on one’s laurels.monolingual: Fig. to stop trying because one is satisfied with one’s past achievements. _ Despite our success, this is no time to rest on our laurels. _ We rested on our laurels too long. Our competitors took away a lot of our business.
examples: Despite our success, this is no time to rest on our laurels.

rest something against something.monolingual: to lean or position something against something, allowing it to bear part of the weight of the thing being rested. _ Rest the heavy end of the box against the wall and we’ll slide it down the stairs. _ Please rest the board against something solid wh
examples: Rest the heavy end of the box against the wall and we’ll slide it down the stairs.

rest with someone or something.monolingual: to remain with someone or something; to be vested with someone or something. _The final decision rests with you. _The power rests with the board of directors.
examples: The final decision rests with you.

restore something to someone.monolingual: to give something back to someone; to cause something to be returned to someone. _ I will restore the man’s wallet to him after we lock the thief up. _ His wallet was restored to him by a police officer.
examples: I will restore the man’s wallet to him after we lock the thief up.

restore something to something.monolingual: to bring something to its original state. _ The state restored the park to its original condition. _ The government forced the mining company to restore the area to its original state.
examples: The state restored the park to its original condition.

restrain someone from something.monolingual: to prevent someone from doing something. _ I had to restrain her from hurting herself. _ I was unable to restrain myself from giggling at the wisecrack.
examples: I had to restrain her from hurting herself.

result from something.monolingual: to emerge from something; to be the outcome of something. _ It will be interesting to see what results from your efforts. _ Nothing resulted from all that work.
examples: It will be interesting to see what results from your efforts.

result in something.monolingual: to achieve something; to bring about something; to cause something to happen. _ I hope that this will result in the police finding your car. _All my effort resulted in nothing at all.
examples: I hope that this will result in the police finding your car.

retail at something.monolingual: to sell at a retail price of something. _ This model normally retails at a much higher price. _What does a product like this usually retail at?
examples: This model normally retails at a much higher price.

retail for something.monolingual: to sell for a retail price of an amount of money. _ This item retails for less than ten dollars. _ How much does this retail for?
examples: This item retails for less than ten dollars.

retail something to someone.monolingual: to sell something to someone at a retail price. _ I can retail this merchandise at ninety percent of the price of my competitor. _We are not allowed to retail this to anyone in the state of Maine.
examples: I can retail this merchandise at ninety percent of the price of my competitor.

retaliate against someone or something.monolingual: to take revenge against someone or something. _The striking workers will retaliate against the company with a protest march. _ The students retaliated against the administration.
examples: The striking workers will retaliate against the company with a protest march.

retire from something.monolingual: to withdraw from something. (Usually to terminate a working career permanently.) _ I retired from the company early. _ When do you intend to retire from your job?
examples: I retired from the company early.

retire on something.monolingual: to quit working and live on something or a particular amount of money. _I already have enough money to retire on. _ I cannot retire on a sum like that!
examples: I already have enough money to retire on.

retire to some place.monolingual: to quit working permanently and move to a particular location. _ When I quit working, I want to retire to Florida. _ We will retire to our place in the country.
examples: When I quit working, I want to retire to Florida.

retool for something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to set up with new or altered tools for a different kind of production. _The factory was closed down so they could retool for next year’s model. _ How soon can we retool for this new line of products?
examples: The factory was closed down so they could retool for next year’s model.

retool something for something.monolingual: to set up a factory with new or altered tools for a different kind of production. _ The manager decided to retool the factory for greater efficiency. _ We will retool the plant for next year’s models.
examples: The manager decided to retool the factory for greater efficiency.

retrieve something from someone.monolingual: to get something back from someone. _ I hope I can retrieve my book from the person who borrowed it. _We were not able to retrieve the lawn mower from Fred before he moved away and took it with him.
examples: I hope I can retrieve my book from the person who borrowed it.

return from some place.monolingual: to come back from some place. _ I just returned from a research trip in the Amazon basin. _ When will they return from their vacation?
examples: I just returned from a research trip in the Amazon basin.

return something for something.monolingual: to give or pay back something for something. _ The clerk returned the correct change for a twenty-dollar bill. _ I hope that the product returns good value for my money.
examples: The clerk returned the correct change for a twenty-dollar bill.

return the favor.monolingual: to do a good deed for someone who has done a good deed for you. _ You helped me last week, so I’ll return the favor and help you this week. _ There is no point in helping Bill. He’ll never return the favor.
examples: You helped me last week, so I’ll return the favor and help you this week.

return to some place.monolingual: to go or come back to some place. _ When do you plan to return to your home? _ I will return there when I have finished here.
examples: I will return there when I have finished here.

return with something.monolingual: to come back with something. _ He went to town and returned with the doctor just in time. _ She returned with the material they had requested.
examples: He went to town and returned with the doctor just in time.

rev something up†.monolingual: to make an idling engine run very fast, in short bursts of power. _ Hey! Stop revving it up! _ I wish that Tom wouldn’t sit out in front of our house in his car and rev up his engine.
examples: I wish that Tom wouldn’t sit out in front of our house in his car and rev up his engine.

rev up.monolingual: to increase in amount or activity. _ Production revved up after the strike. _We’re hoping business will rev up soon.
examples: Production revved up after the strike.

revel in something.monolingual: to rejoice or celebrate about something. _ All the children reveled in the fresh, warm, spring air. _ Tony reveled in his success.
examples: All the children reveled in the fresh, warm, spring air.

revenge is sweet..monolingual: Prov. It is very pleasurable to revenge yourself on someone. _ Jill: Remember when Tom left me for another woman? Well, she just left him, and he asked me out on a date. I told him I had better things to do. Jane: Revenge is sweet, huh?
examples: Jill: Remember when Tom left me for another woman? Well, she just left him, and he asked me out on a date.

reverberate through something.monolingual: [for sound] to roll through or pass through a space. _ The thunder reverberated through the valley. _The sound of the organ reverberated through the church.
examples: The thunder reverberated through the valley.

reverberate throughout something.monolingual: [for sound] to roll about and fill a space. _ The thunder reverberated throughout the valley. _ The noise of chairs scraping the f loor reverberated throughout the room.
examples: The thunder reverberated throughout the valley.

reverberate with something.monolingual: to echo or resound with something. _ The hall reverberated with the rich basso voice of Walter Rogers. _The church reverberated with the roar of the pipe organ.
examples: The hall reverberated with the rich basso voice of Walter Rogers.

revert to someone or something.monolingual: 1. to return to some type of person or a former state. _ After he was out of prison, he reverted to a life of crime. _ She quickly reverted to her childhood dialect after a few weeks at home.
examples: After he was out of prison, he reverted to a life of crime.

review for something.monolingual: to study material again for something, such as an examination. _ I need some time to review for the examination. _ Have you had enough time to review for your speech?
examples: I need some time to review for the examination.

revolt against someone or something.monolingual: to rebel or rise against someone or something. _ The citizens were gathering arms, preparing to revolt against the government.
examples: The citizens were gathering arms, preparing to revolt against the government.

revolted at someone or something.monolingual: sickened by someone or something. _ I was revolted at Frank and his behavior. _ We were all revolted at the scene of the bloody highway accident.
examples: I was revolted at Frank and his behavior.

reward someone for something.monolingual: to give someone a prize or a bonus for doing something. _I would like to reward you for your honesty. _ She wanted to reward herself for her hard work, so she treated herself to a massage.
examples: I would like to reward you for your honesty.

reward someone with something.monolingual: to honor someone with a gift of something. _ She rewarded the helpful child with a chocolate chip cookie. _He rewarded himself with a night on the town.
examples: She rewarded the helpful child with a chocolate chip cookie.

rhapsodize over someone or something.monolingual: to go on and on about the virtues of someone or something. _ Young Thomas likes to rhapsodize over Francine, his girlfriend. _ Please do not rhapsodize over this poem anymore.
examples: Young Thomas likes to rhapsodize over Francine, his girlfriend.

rhyme something with something.monolingual: [for someone] to make one word rhyme with another word. _ I need to rhyme tree with some other word. Any suggestions? _Can I rhyme good with food?
examples: I need to rhyme tree with some other word.

rhyme with something.monolingual: [for a word] to rhyme with another word. _ You can’t use house in that line of the poem, because it doesn’t rhyme with mice. _The last word in your poem doesn’t rhyme with any other word in the poem!
examples: You can’t use house in that line of the poem, because it doesn’t rhyme with mice.

rich in something.monolingual: having valuable resources, characteristics, traditions, or history. _ The entire region is rich in historical churches. _ Our soil is rich in important nutrients.
examples: The entire region is rich in historical churches.

rich with something.monolingual: having a lot of something; abundant in something. _ The beautiful book was rich with color illustrations. _ The old town was rich with elegant Victorian houses.
examples: The beautiful book was rich with color illustrations.

ricochet off something.monolingual: [for some rapidly moving object, such as a bullet] to bounce off something at an angle. _ The bullet ricocheted off the wall and struck the gunman. _ Bullets were ricocheting off the walls from all angles.
examples: The bullet ricocheted off the wall and struck the gunman.

*rid of someone or something.monolingual: free of someone or something. (*Typically: be ~; get ~.) _I’m trying to get rid of Mr. Smith. He’s bothering me. _ I’ll be happy when I get rid of my old car.
examples: I’m trying to get rid of Mr.

ride away.monolingual: to depart, riding a bike or a horse or similar animal. _She got on her horse and rode away. _They rode away without even saying good-bye.
examples: She got on her horse and rode away.

ride by someone or something.monolingual: to pass by someone or something, riding. (As on a horse or bicycle, or as a passenger in a car.) _ She rode by me without saying anything. _ I rode by the store and forget to stop and go in.
examples: She rode by me without saying anything.

ride off.monolingual: to depart, riding something such as a horse or a bicycle. _Betty said good-bye and rode off. _We rode off, each one in a different direction.
examples: Betty said good-bye and rode off.

ride off in all directions.monolingual: 1. Fig. [for people] to scatter, riding something, such as a horse or a bicycle. _The boys hopped on their bikes and rode off in all directions. _ The sheriff got the posse together and they rode off in all directions, looking for the bank robber.
examples: The boys hopped on their bikes and rode off in all directions.

ride on.monolingual: to continue to ride, traveling onward. _ We rode on for at least an hour before finding a rest stop. _ They rode on for a while.
examples: We rode on for at least an hour before finding a rest stop.

ride on something.monolingual: 1. Lit. to travel on something. _Do you like to ride on the train? _ I have never ridden on a horse.
examples: I have never ridden on a horse.

ride over someone or something.monolingual: to pass over someone or something, riding something such as a horse or a bicycle. _ Bobby fell down and Susan rode over him with her bicycle, but he wasn’t hurt at all. _ Tom almost rode over my toe!
examples: Bobby fell down and Susan rode over him with her bicycle, but he wasn’t hurt at all.

ride someone about something.monolingual: to continue to bother someone about something. _ Stop riding me about my weight! This is how I’m supposed to be! _ It’s not fair to ride someone about being bald.
examples: It’s not fair to ride someone about being bald.

ride something down.monolingual: to ride on something that is going down, such as an elevator. _You take the stairs, and I will ride the elevator down. _ I don’t want to ride the cable car down. I will walk.
examples: You take the stairs, and I will ride the elevator down.

ride something out†.monolingual: to endure something unpleasant. (Originally referred to ships lasting out a storm.) _It was a nasty situation, but the mayor tried to ride it out. _ The mayor decided to ride out the scandal.
examples: It was a nasty situation, but the mayor tried to ride it out.

ride the gravy train.monolingual: Fig. to live in ease or luxury. _ If I had a million dollars, I sure could ride the gravy train. _ I wouldn’t like loafing if I were rich. I don’t want to ride the gravy train.
examples: If I had a million dollars, I sure could ride the gravy train.

ride to some place.monolingual: to travel to a place, riding something such as a horse or a bicycle, or a vehicle one does not drive. _ I will ride to town and get the doctor. _ Tom will ride to the store on his bike to get a loaf of bread.
examples: I will ride to town and get the doctor.

ride with someone.monolingual: to travel with someone on or in a vehicle or a beast of burden. _ I’m going to the store for some milk. Do you want to ride with me? _ Can I ride with you to the store?
examples: I’m going to the store for some milk.

riding for a fall.monolingual: Fig. risking failure or an accident, usually due to overconfidence. _ Tom drives too fast, and he seems too sure of himself. He’s riding for a fall. _Bill needs to eat better and get more sleep. He’s riding for a fall.
examples: Tom drives too fast, and he seems too sure of himself.

rifle through something.monolingual: to ransack something; to search quickly or roughly through something looking for something. _ The teenager quickly rif led through the cabinets, looking for something worth eating. _ The soldiers rif led through every house they could break into.
examples: The teenager quickly rif led through the cabinets, looking for something worth eating.

rig something up†.monolingual: to prepare something, perhaps on short notice or without the proper materials. _ We don’t have what’s needed to make the kind of circuit you have described, but I think we can rig something up anyway. _ We will rig up whatever you need.
examples: We don’t have what’s needed to make the kind of circuit you have described, but I think we can rig something up anyway.

*right as rain.monolingual: Cliché perfectly fine; all right. (Based on the alliteration with r. *Also: as ~.) _ Lily has sprained her ankle, but after a few weeks of rest she should be as right as rain. _All we need to do is tidy the house up; then it will be right as rain.
examples: Lily has sprained her ankle, but after a few weeks of rest she should be as right as rain.

right in the kisser.monolingual: Inf. right in the mouth or face. _ Wilbur poked the cop right in the kisser. _ He caught a punch right in the kisser.
examples: Wilbur poked the cop right in the kisser.
